subtitle: A quiet-rebellion fundraiser to protect Pacific Northwest scrubland from clearcut.
brief:
Build a one-page site for "Adopt an Acre" — a quiet-rebellion fundraiser to protect Pacific Northwest scrubland from clearcut.

The page features THREE looping hero videos in sequence (a 3-shot arc: weathered hands on a sapling → wide lone figure in a cleared field with bulldozer tracks → first leaf catching wind at dawn) and a prominent "Adopt an Acre" button linking to https://example.com/donate.
visual_bible: Pacific Northwest scrubland, overcast cool-gray skies with occasional shafts of weak sun. Mist clinging to low ground. Moss, bracken, second-growth fir at the edges, but in the foreground: raw cleared earth with bulldozer track ruts and a single sapling. Shot on 35mm film, naturalistic light, no color grading toward heroism. Documentary stillness — NOT activist-anthem, NOT mournful-orchestral. Damp earth tones, mossy greens, a single warm note (skin, leaf-edge) against the gray. 16:9.
shots: HOOK: Weathered hands cradling a small sapling, fingers pressing soil around its roots, breath visible in cold air.
ESCALATION: Wide on a lone figure standing in a cleared field, bulldozer tracks crisscrossing the foreground, distant treeline cut sharply against the gray sky.
PAYOFF: Close on a single new leaf at dawn catching the first thin wind, a warm edge of sun barely lighting it from behind.
palette_hint: damp earth tones and mossy greens with a single warm-amber accent
